info.title: Patent Status API
info.description:
Status of every US patent application and patent, served from our own copy of USPTO bulk data (public domain,
17 U.S.C. §105). Built for AI agents: compact JSON, stable field names, no seats, no rate limits per key.

**How to use**: send `X-API-KEY: <key>` (or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`) on every `/v1` request.
No key yet? `POST /agent/signup` with your owner's email returns one; the first data request answers
`402 {"error": "payment_required", "checkout": "POST /agent/checkout-link", "minimum_usd": 20}` — call that endpoint,
have a human pay the Stripe link, and retry. Read `/agents.md` for the full flow.

**Billing**: 1 unit per request; list endpoints 1 unit per 100 rows returned. Only successful (2xx) responses are
charged. `X-Credits-Charged` on every response says what it cost (`0` on an error); a charged one also carries
`X-Credits-Remaining`, your balance after it.

**Provenance**: every object carries `source` {product, file_date} naming the USPTO bulk file it came from,
`as_of` (the date we last ingested that table) and `stale` (true when our copy is older than the product's cadence allows: 48 h, or a week and a day for the weekly maintenance-fee file — check
`/health`). Application numbers are 8-digit strings; patent numbers are strings without commas; dates are ISO 8601.

**Typical flows**: name → `/v1/entities/search` → `/v1/entities/{id}/applications?status=pending`;
application → `/v1/applications/{n}` then `/transactions?since=` to watch for office actions and allowances;
patent → `/v1/patents/{n}/maintenance` (alive?) and `/v1/patents/{n}/ptab` (challenged?).

get.summary: Claims, abstract and CPC of a granted patent
get.description: Answers: what does this granted patent actually claim, what is it about, and how is it classified. Returns `claims` [{number, text, dependent_on}] (dependent_on lists the claims a dependent claim refers to; empty for independent claims; `canceled: true` marks claims canceled by amendment, `number_raw` flags a claim USPTO mis-numbered), `independent_claims`, `claim_count`, `canceled_claims`, `abstract`, `cpc` (CPC symbols as classified at issue, main first), `title`, `kind`, `application_number`, `date`. Text comes from USPTO's weekly full-text XML; a number outside the weeks we hold is a 404 whose `detail` states the covered dates — the status endpoints cover every application regardless. Costs 1 request.

get.summary: What a patent cites, and who cites it
get.description: Answers: what prior art is on this patent's front page, and which later patents cite it. `backward` is the front-page list grouped by what was cited — `patents` (US, canonical numbers), `publications` (US pre-grant, US20130157853A1), `foreign` (country + number as printed), `npl` (non-patent literature text) — each with `category` (examiner | applicant | other, with `category_detail` for other) and the cited document's `date` at the precision USPTO prints (usually a month), plus `count` / `examiner_count` / `applicant_count`. `forward` is every loaded grant citing this patent number, newest number first: [{patent_number, grant_date, title, categories}] with `count` (distinct citing grants) and `next_cursor` (famous patents have thousands; page with `limit`/`cursor`). A reference USPTO printed unreadably is kept verbatim with a `defect` note. `direction` = both | backward | forward. Coverage is the weekly grant files loaded: a `forward.count` is complete for those weeks only, and `backward` is null with `detail` naming the covered dates when the patent's own grant file is not loaded. Citations of the patent's pre-grant publication are not folded in. Costs 1 request per 100 citation rows returned.

post.summary: Status of many applications in one call
post.description: Answers: what is the status of each of these applications — the `status` block, patent/publication numbers and applicant for up to 1,000 application numbers, in request order; a number we do not hold comes back in `not_found`, one that cannot be an application number in `invalid`, as you wrote it. Costs 1 request per 100 rows returned. Use /v1/applications/{n} for the full object.

get.summary: What happened, as a feed you can poll
get.description: Answers: what happened to these applications / patents / entities since I last looked — office actions, allowances, abandonments, grants, publications, assignments, PTAB petitions, maintenance events — as detected by our nightly ingest. Filter by `types` and/or targets (at least one filter is required); page with `cursor`; use `since` (ISO date or datetime, on detected_at) for 'since my last poll'. The webhook alternative is POST /v1/monitors. Costs 1 request per 100 rows.

get.summary: Prosecution timeline of one application
get.description: Answers: what has happened to this application and when — every USPTO transaction (filing, office actions, responses, notice of allowance, issue, abandonment), newest first. Each item is {date, code, description, event_type} where code/description are USPTO's verbatim and event_type is our normalized enum (office_action, allowance, abandonment, grant, publication, ... or null). Pass `since=YYYY-MM-DD` to get only what happened on or after a date (e.g. since your last check).

get.summary: Office actions (examiner rejections) of one application, with text
get.description: Answers: what did the examiner reject, under which statutes, and when is a response due. Each item is one office action (non-final, final, restriction, ...) with mailed_date, the reply deadline per 37 CFR 1.134 / MPEP 710.02(b) (`response_due_estimate`, `response_due_max` with extensions under 1.136(a), `response_period_months`, `response_extendable`, `restarts_period` — all null for an action whose period is set in the letter; on a notice of allowance the estimate is the issue-fee due date), `statutes` and `rejections` when USPTO's parsed data exists — `statutes` carries the bare section beside any paragraphed form (103, 112, 112(a)) so a filter on '103' never misses, and is null rather than empty when USPTO sent no structured rejections at all, which is not the same as an action that rejected nothing. The examiner's prose — `body_text` and the per-statute rejection text inside `sections` — costs include_text=true (tens of KB each); without it `text_chars` and `section_chars` say how much there is to ask for. Text lags mailing by 0–7 days; a transaction can exist before its text does.

get.description: Answers: who owns this application, and how did ownership change — every recorded assignment (reel/frame) whose properties include this application or the patent granted on it, newest recorded first. Each has `assignors`, `assignees` (with `entity_id` when resolved), `conveyance_type` (assignment, security interest, merger, ...), `recorded_date`, `execution_date`, and the `properties` covered by that recordation.

get.summary: Current status of one application
get.description: Answers: what is the current state of this US patent application — pending, allowed, abandoned, or granted (and as which patent), who filed it, who examines it, what it claims priority to, and how much activity (office actions, assignments, PTAB challenges) it has seen. One object: `status` {code, description, category, date}, `patent_number`/`grant_date` (null until granted), `publication_number`/`publication_date`, `applicant_name` + `applicant_entity_id` (use with /v1/entities), `examiner_name`, `art_unit`, `entity_status` (small|micro|undiscounted), `continuity` {parents, children}, `counts`, and provenance `source` {product, file_date} / `as_of` / `stale`. For the timeline call /transactions; for ownership call /assignments. 404 not_found if we have no record.

get.summary: PTAB challenges against one patent
get.description: Answers: is this patent under (or has it survived) an inter partes review, post-grant review, CBM or derivation proceeding at the PTAB, and what did the Board decide. Each proceeding has `type`, `petitioner`, `patent_owner`, `filed_date`, `status`, `instituted` (true|false|null), `claims_outcome` (all_unpatentable|some_unpatentable|none_unpatentable|null, from the final written decision), `final_decision_date`, and `decisions` — every Board decision document with `kind` (institution_granted, institution_denied, final_written_decision, termination, rehearing, appeal_mandate, other), `date`, `outcome`, `statutes`, `issue_types`, `title`, `pdf_url`. Pass include_text=true for each decision's text as USPTO's dataset carries it (a preview of a few hundred characters). Empty `proceedings` for a known patent means no challenge on record.

get.summary: Is this patent alive? Maintenance fees and expiration
get.description: Answers: is this patent still in force, have its 3.5/7.5/11.5-year maintenance fees been paid, and when does it expire. Returns `events` (every fee event: paid, reminder, expired, reinstated), `windows` {"3.5y", "7.5y", "11.5y": paid|due|expired|n/a}, `expired` (true once a fee lapsed or the term ended), `expiration_reason`, and `expiration_estimate` (`term_start` + 20 years + PTA, where `term_start` is the earliest filing date the patent claims benefit from under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c), else its own filing date; `estimate: true` because terminal disclaimers may shorten it). Window values: paid, due (payable now), grace (overdue, surcharge), expired, upcoming (not yet payable), n/a (design/plant/reissue owe no fees); `deadlines` carries each window's opens/due/surcharge_until dates and `next_fee` the first unpaid window (null when the patent is not alive).

get.summary: Resolve a company or inventor name to an entity id
get.description: Answers: which entity is 'Impossible Foods' (or any assignee / inventor name) in the USPTO record, and what are its known name variants. Start here before /v1/entities/{id}/applications, /v1/assignments?assignee=, or /v1/ptab?patent_owner=. Results are ranked (prefix matches first) and include `aliases`, `location`, and `counts` {applications, patents, pending}. A company printed under several names is one row with a `fam_...` family id and `members`; a family id is accepted wherever an entity id is. `type` filters to assignee or inventor. Costs 1 unit per 100 rows.

get.summary: An entity's applications (portfolio), filterable by status
get.description: Answers: what has this company filed, and what is each filing's state right now. Each row carries the application's current `status` {code, description, category, bucket, date}, `patent_number` when granted, and the link `role`/`confidence`. `status` filters on USPTO's raw category: pending, granted, abandoned, allowed, expired, provisional, pct, other. `status.bucket` is what /v1/entities/{id}/stats counts (allowed folds into pending, expired-after-grant into granted, never-examined into other, null for an application we do not hold), so count buckets to reconcile a portfolio against the statistics. Newest serial first; paginate with `next_cursor`. Costs 1 unit per 100 rows.

get.summary: What is this company doing: portfolio size, velocity, prosecution, technology, examiners, PTAB exposure, deals
get.description: Answers: how big is this company's US patent position, is it growing, how well does it prosecute, what technology is it in, who examines it, is it under attack at the PTAB, and is it buying or selling patents. One object of blocks — `portfolio` {applications, patents, pending, granted, abandoned, alive_patents, expiring_within_12_months, computed_over}, `velocity` {filings_per_year, grants_per_year: [{year, n}]}, `prosecution` (the same metrics as /v1/examiners/{name}/stats over this entity's applications: allowance_rate, median_months_to_first_action, median_months_to_grant, avg_office_actions_per_disposed, rce_rate, appeal_rate), `where` {cpc_subclasses [{subclass, n, share}], cpc_coverage, art_units}, `who` {examiners [{name, key, n}], prosecuted_by {customer_numbers}}, `ptab` {as_patent_owner {proceedings, instituted, claims_lost}, as_petitioner}, `ownership` {acquired, sold, since} — every number defined in `definitions`. Portfolio membership is that of /v1/entities/{id}/applications (title per recorded assignments beats filing). Rates are null when undefined; read `cpc_coverage` before trusting the subclasses. Large entities are precomputed nightly, the rest on first request (`computed_at`); 504 computation_timeout means the entity is queued for the next nightly run. Costs 1 request.

get.summary: How does this examiner prosecute: allowance rate, time to first action, RCE and appeal rates
get.description: Answers: what are my odds and how long will it take with this examiner. Precomputed nightly over every application the examiner is listed on: `counts` by status (pending, granted, abandoned, other), `allowance_rate`, `median_months_to_first_action`, `median_months_to_disposal`, `avg_office_actions_per_disposed`, `rce_rate`, `appeal_rate`, `art_units`, plus `sample_size`, `computed_over` (filing-date range) and `definitions`. The name is matched case- and whitespace-insensitively ('smith, jane' = 'SMITH, JANE'). 404 not_found when there are no statistics for that name yet: the tables are rebuilt nightly, so a newly listed examiner appears the next day; USPTO's docket placeholders ('CENTRAL, DOCKET') never do.

get.summary: Find patents and applications by keywords, CPC class, filing date and owner
get.description: Answers: which granted patents / published applications are about X — by words in the title, abstract or claims (`q`, websearch syntax: words are ANDed, "quoted phrases" must be adjacent, `-word` excludes, `or` alternates; English stemming), and/or in a CPC level (`cpc`: C, C12, C12N, C12N15 or C12N15/88 — one level, not a free-form prefix), optionally only `doc_type` grant|publication, filed within `filed_after`..`filed_before` (inclusive, on the application's filing date), and/or in one entity's portfolio (`entity_id` from /v1/entities/search). At least one of q / cpc / entity_id is required (400 otherwise). This is keyword search over the weekly full-text products, not similarity or prior-art search. Each result: `doc_number`, `doc_type`, `kind`, `application_number`, `title`, `date` (grant/publication), `filing_date`, `cpc`, `snippet` (abstract with **matches** marked) and `rank` (ts_rank_cd; null without q). Ranked best first, then newest; page with `next_cursor`. `total` is the number of matches up to 10,000 (`total_capped: true` beyond). A query that runs longer than 10 s is a 504 computation_timeout: add a cpc level, doc_type, a date range or more specific words.
